conversation.text: I want a simple fighting game with fist fighting animations from the Marketplace, a practice dummy to test on, VFX and SFX when attacking, and a hit counter that goes up every time I hit the dummy.

Player throws punches at a practice dummy using ready-made fist-fighting animations, watching the hit counter climb with each connecting punch while VFX and SFX confirm every hit. The rising counter gives a simple, satisfying way to test and repeat combos.

proposal.title: Fist Fighter Practice
proposal.playerExperience: Player throws punches at a practice dummy using ready-made fist-fighting animations, watching the hit counter climb with each connecting punch while VFX and SFX confirm every hit. The rising counter gives a simple, satisfying way to test and repeat combos.
proposal.visualDirection: A small practice arena with one stationary dummy, using Marketplace fist-fighting animation packs for punches, plus small impact particle bursts and punch sound effects on contact.
assumptions: Punch animations come from a generic Marketplace fist-fighting animation pack rather than a specific named asset.
The dummy is stationary, cannot be defeated, and simply absorbs hits indefinitely for practice purposes.
The hit counter is a simple on-screen number that increases by 1 per successful punch and does not reset unless the player restarts the game.
Single-player only, with the dummy as the sole target—no additional opponents.

firstPlaytest.goal: Confirm that punching the dummy triggers animation, VFX, and SFX together, and that the hit counter only increases on actual contact.
steps: Walk up to the dummy and press the punch action
Punch the dummy several times in a row
Step away from the dummy and punch empty air
Stand still without pressing punch
firstPlaytest.expected: The player can reliably land hits on the dummy, see and hear feedback each time, and watch the hit counter accurately track only successful punches.

checks.expected: Punch animation plays, a hit VFX and SFX trigger, and the hit counter increases by 1
The counter increases by 1 each time, matching the number of connecting punches
The punch animation plays but no VFX, SFX, or counter increase occurs since there's no contact
The counter stays unchanged, confirming it only rises from actual hits
